title: Four o’clock, the plan comes back
caption: Early, polished, and completely sure.

confident-and-wrong.header: Confident and wrong looks the same
confident-and-wrong.description: In the BCG study, on a task built to lie outside the model’s ability, AI users were 19 points less likely to be correct, and their wrong answers read as coherent. The task was designed to fail, so this shows a mechanism, not a typical rate.[1]

delegating-raises-confidence.description: In a 47-person study, programmers with an AI assistant wrote less secure code and were more likely to believe it secure.[1] Disputed: a 58-person study found a gap of at most about 10%, and both used 2021 to 2022 models.[2]

insecure-code-with-ai-assistants.title: Do Users Write More Insecure Code with AI Assistants?

lost-at-c.title: Lost at C: A User Study on the Security Implications of Large Language Model Code Assistants

gatekeeper.description: A New York court fined lawyers $5,000 for filing six cases ChatGPT invented, and wrote that using AI is not improper but rules “impose a gatekeeping role on attorneys”.[1]

mata-v-avianca.title: Mata v. Avianca, Inc., Opinion and Order

the-plan-lands.title: The plan lands
the-plan-lands.script: It is four o'clock. The plan comes back, early. It is polished. Venue, menu, timeline, even a playlist. And it is written with total confidence.

one-line-is-off.title: One line is off
one-line-is-off.script: You start reading. And one line is off. The venue it picked is already booked that weekend. Or the budget has one zero too many. It does not say maybe. It says it in the same calm voice as everything else.

you-catch-it-or-not.title: You catch it, or you do not
you-catch-it-or-not.script: So now it is on you. If you read with a pen in your hand, you catch it. If you skim, because it all looks so sure of itself, it goes straight to the CEO. The confidence sounds the same whether the line is right or wrong. Only your eye can tell the two apart.
